summary: Reviewed 4 files: gui/api-knowledge.ts, src/storage/knowledge-store.ts, src/schema/knowledge.ts, gui/server.ts. 0 Critical, 0 High, 1 Medium (defence-in-depth gap — documented), 2 Low findings. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: MEDIUM — A03 Injection / A04 Insecure Design (defence-in-depth gap): handleDeleteKnowledge (api-knowledge.ts:265) and handlePromoteKnowledge (api-knowledge.ts:320) accept repository_name as a raw string from query parameters. Neither handler applies PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX at the handler level before passing the value to KnowledgeStoreManager. The storage layer's repositoryStorePath() calls _validateSlug() (knowledge-store.ts:516), which tests against PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX and throws a generic Error for non-conforming slugs — making path traversal impossible in practice. However, this generic Error is not caught as an ApiError, so a malformed slug (e.g. '../evil') would propagate to the server's unhandled-error branch, returning a 500 instead of a 400 VALIDATION_ERROR. Recommendation: add an explicit PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX check in handleDeleteKnowledge and handlePromoteKnowledge (mirroring the pattern already used in KnowledgeMoveBodySchema) to (1) ensure path traversal is rejected at the earliest possible layer, (2) return a semantically correct 400 VALIDATION_ERROR rather than 500, and (3) remove reliance on the storage layer as the sole regex guard for these two handlers. Contrast: handleMoveKnowledge and handleUpdateKnowledge use KnowledgeMoveBodySchema/KnowledgeUpdateBodySchema respectively, which both embed z.string().regex(PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX) — so this gap is specific to the two query-param-based handlers.

LOW — A01 Broken Access Control (observation): The knowledge API is entirely unauthenticated. All five endpoints (list, update, delete, promote, move) operate purely on ledgerRoot, which is a server-side path supplied at process startup. Since the server binds to localhost only (CORS: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost:<port>), and all knowledge data is local developer tooling, the absence of auth is an accepted design trade-off for this tool category. Recorded for awareness; no remediation required for this threat model.

LOW — A05 Security Misconfiguration (observation): CORS is restricted to http://localhost:<port> (server.ts:104-109) — same-origin only. Security headers are applied on all responses: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and a restrictive CSP (default-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'). The server is localhost-only tooling with no TLS required. Configuration is correctly hardened for the intended deployment context.

LOW — A09 Security Logging (observation): Unhandled errors in the knowledge route handlers are logged to process.stderr with route context (e.g. '[server] Unhandled error in PATCH /api/knowledge/:id: ...'). ApiError instances are mapped to structured JSON error responses without leaking internal details (sendError serialises only {error: {code, message}} — no stack traces). The storage layer's _validateSlug() generic Error, noted above as the medium finding, would currently surface as a 500 with the generic 'An unexpected error occurred.' message — no internal path or slug value is leaked to the client. Logging coverage is adequate for this tool.

Minor inconsistency: handleUpdateKnowledge and handleDeleteKnowledge use msg.includes('not found') to map storage errors to NOT_FOUND ApiErrors, while handlePromoteKnowledge and handleMoveKnowledge use msg.toLowerCase().includes('not found'). The storage layer consistently emits lowercase 'not found' in all error messages, so both forms work correctly. Recommend normalising all four handlers to use the .toLowerCase() form for defensive consistency — but this is cosmetic and does not affect behaviour.

Follow-up hardening ticket recommended: handleDeleteKnowledge and handlePromoteKnowledge accept repository_name as a raw query-parameter string without applying PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX at the handler level. The security auditor confirmed the gap is safe in practice (the storage layer's _validateSlug() blocks path traversal), but a malformed slug will surface as a 500 instead of a 400 VALIDATION_ERROR. Adding an explicit regex guard mirroring the pattern in KnowledgeMoveBodySchema/KnowledgeUpdateBodySchema would (1) return semantically correct 400 errors, (2) eliminate reliance on the storage layer as the sole regex guard for these two handlers, and (3) align the validation discipline across all five handlers.

[documentation-forward] The JSDoc for handleDeleteKnowledge (api-knowledge.ts ~line 248) and handlePromoteKnowledge (api-knowledge.ts ~line 304) should document the defence-in-depth gap as a known limitation with a note that PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX is enforced at the storage layer via _validateSlug() rather than at the handler level. This will help future contributors understand why a malformed slug returns 500 and where to add the guard if the behaviour is later hardened.

[documentation-forward] The module-level JSDoc (api-knowledge.ts lines 1-16) lists the four error codes and their HTTP mappings but does not document the ID-change behaviour on promote/move — the returned insight has a different numeric ID than the original (assigned by the target store's next_id counter).
